elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "SFJ hereby represents and warrants that (a) the SFJ Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner..."

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Inserted limb (b): "any software provided by SFJ under this Agreement will conform to its documentation". The scope limiter ("any software provided by SFJ") is a condition on applicability, not an undefined trigger; the Agreement identifies no SFJ deliverables, so the software limb is the operative documentation warranty.

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: Inserted limb (b) sets "a period of ninety (90) days following delivery", not 12 months.
Inserted limb (a): "for a period of ninety (90) days following performance, will conform in all material respects to the requirements of this Agreement".

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "SFJ will, at its option, re-perform, repair or replace the non-conforming SFJ Services or software".
"...or refund to PB the amounts paid for them."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: The inserted warranty contains no compliance-with-laws undertaking, and Section 13.5 covers only sufficiency of funds.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious-code warranty appears anywhere in the rendered Article 13 language.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "any software provided by SFJ under this Agreement will conform to its documentation for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery" \u2014 an express software-to-documentation warranty at the 90-day floor.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: Limb (a) warrants the SFJ Services for "ninety (90) days following performance", exceeding the 30-day floor; placement inside Article 13 means the Section 13.6.2 carve-out ("EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SET FORTH IN THIS ARTICLE 13") preserves it.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "SFJ will, at its option, re-perform, repair or replace the non-conforming SFJ Services or software".
"...or refund to PB the amounts paid for them." Remedy applies to "any breach of this warranty", covering both limbs.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: an express services warranty (90 days, above the 30-day floor), an express software-to-documentation warranty (90 days), and repair/replace plus refund remedies, all inserted inside Article 13 so the Section 13.6.2 disclaimer carve-out preserves them. Preferred fails on the 12-month software period, compliance with laws, and no malicious code.

Minimality defect 1: the services warranty is drafted at ninety (90) days when the chosen fallback checklist requires only 30 days. Exceeding the fallback numeric threshold without necessity fails minimality \u2014 either set the services limb to thirty (30) days or justify the longer period by targeting the preferred level.

Minimality defect 2: the "performed in a professional and workmanlike manner" limb is a preferred-level element outside the selected fallback checklist and is not required to make the 30-day services conformance warranty operative; it should be dropped if the fallback is the target, or the finding should be re-pitched at preferred.
Intent is preserved: the insertion sits between 13.5 and 13.6.2 within Article 13, creates no dangling cross-reference, and does not contradict the retained funding covenant or the mutual disclaimer.

Drafting fixes to make the insertion clean: (i) give the new paragraph a section number (e.g. 13.5.1 or 13.5A) so the Article 13 carve-out in 13.6.2 is unambiguous, and (ii) confirm "SFJ Services" is a defined term in Article 1 \u2014 it is not among the resolved definitions supplied, and an undefined capitalised scope term would leave the warranty's subject matter open.
